art_direction.focal_hierarchy: The phone, the paid mark or the jar first, the ticket or the tag second, the stamps and cards third, the room and window last.

hero.finish: Lit upper-left tungsten on the pass and table, cool glow on the phone screen, scuffed steel, a flame with a heat shimmer, glass highlights on the jar and soft contact shadows.
hero.silhouette: A rounded off-white phone over a table code, a boxy ticket printer with a paper slot and a rail of tickets, a wok on a flame at a steel pass and a glass tip jar.

lighting.motivation: Warm tungsten pendant light from the upper left over the tables and paper, cool screen glow from the phone and panel, and the wok flame throws its own warm light on the pass.

art_direction.motion_language: Marks travel on lines with continuous acceleration and braking, cards slide and settle without bounce, stamps land once, tags swing and settle, the flame flares and eases, and the camera holds while objects perform.
art_direction.palette_reason: Warm cream paper carries the records, terracotta and brass hold the room, steel gray holds the pass, the off-white phone is the one clean value and a single chili red is kept for the paid mark, the wok flare and the stamps.
art_direction.shape_language: Rounded phone and panel against boxy steel pass, printer and tables, and flat paper cards with worn corners. Nothing is symmetric: the ticket rail leans, the stamp lands crooked, the tag swings.

signature_shot.reason: The paid mark arrives, the ticket prints and the wok flares, the whole pay-first order in one movement.

captions.text: When the only server at Wok and Karahi in Spring walked out,
who was going to take the order?
The family didn't post a job ad.
They put an AI host named Haniya at the front of the house.
A guest scans a code at the table,
Nothing is cooked until the order is paid for.
The owner says the restaurant saves or wins back $9,650 a month,
FOX 26 reports that kitchen staff now get all of the tips.
When the employer takes no tip credit,
federal rules allow a tip pool with cooks.
No report says whether this restaurant takes one.
One customer said QR codes don't suit people like her mother.
So software now takes the order,
and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.

clauses.text: When the only server at Wok and Karahi in Spring walked out,
who was going to take the order?
The family didn't post a job ad.
They put an AI host named Haniya at the front of the house.
A guest scans a code at the table,
Nothing is cooked until the order is paid for.
The owner says the restaurant saves or wins back $9,650 a month,
FOX 26 reports that kitchen staff now get all of the tips.
When the employer takes no tip credit,
federal rules allow a tip pool with cooks.
No report says whether this restaurant takes one.
One customer said QR codes don't suit people like her mother.
So software now takes the order,
and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.

story_contract.action: Replaced its sole server with an AI host that takes orders by table code and phone, with payment first.
story_contract.actor: Wok & Karahi, a family restaurant in Spring, as reported by FOX 26, Muslim Mirror and Click2Houston
story_contract.affected_people: The family, its kitchen staff and guests who order by phone or code. No person is named.
story_contract.change: A server who took the order and ran the check is replaced by a host, and kitchen staff reportedly get all tips.
story_contract.closing_answer: Software now takes the order, and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.
story_contract.consequence: Software takes the order and payment comes first, while savings and tips rest on the owner's account.
story_contract.opening_question: When a restaurant loses its only server, who takes the order?

scenes.advances: The front door swings shut with its bell ringing and the server apron swings on its hook. The host stand phone starts to ring with no one at the stand. Order tickets stay blank on the pad while two tables wait with plates.
A window sign frame stays empty, with no job ad pinned in it. A flat host panel lights up on a stand at the front and the name Haniya writes across it. A tag reading AI host attaches to the panel.
A phone lifts over the table code and its viewfinder locks. The menu opens on the phone screen. A fingertip taps a dish and the chow mein row lights. The pay button turns to a paid mark.

The ticket printer sits idle with a blank slot beside an empty wok on an unlit burner. A paid mark travels along a line from the phone into the printer slot and the lamp turns red. A ticket prints, rises and hangs on the pass rail. A cook loads the wok and the flame flares as the pan starts to cook.
A ledger card slides onto the back desk. The ledger card takes a tag reading $9,650 a month. A stamp reading owner count lands crooked on the card. A receipt clip beside the card stays bare.
Coins and bills drop from the pay screen toward the kitchen pass. They land in the tip jar at the pass and the jar fills. A tag reading FOX 26 reports all to the kitchen hangs on the jar.
A federal rule card slides onto the desk and a no tip credit checkbox appears on it. The cooks line on the rule card lights beside the box. A pen circles the lit cooks line and the box.
The restaurant folder slides beside the rule card. The folder opens and the one box stays blank. A question mark draws beside the blank box.
